newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee dull on overseas lethargy of dlr.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee dull on overseas lethargy of dlr.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee moved in a narrow range on a subdued overseas dollar with banks holding back from building positions, dealers said.
At 0900 GMT the rupee was at 57.53 to the dollar after opening at 57.47. The rupee closed at 57.49 on Tuesday.
"Commercial demand for dollars is being matched with ample supply, which is keeping the exchange rate in a narrow range," said an American Express Bank dealer.
The Central Bank left the exchange rate unchanged and buying and selling prices remained at 56.8805 and 58.0296.
Overseas lethargy of the dollar, which was not good for building positions, was checking the dollar's rise, dealers said.
"There is no reason for the dollar to fall either in the absence of a big inward remittances and fairly stable money rates," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Call money was at 16 percent after opening at 12.4 percent and rising to a high of 16.5, they said.
